newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia UMW says not spoken to Sapura.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia UMW says not spoken to Sapura.

text.p: Malaysian auto distributor UMW Holdings Bhd said on Thursday that it had not received any communication from Sapura Holdings Sdn Bhd regarding a possible acquisition of a stake in UMW by Sapura.

"The Board (of UMW) would like to stress... that the company has not received any communication whatsoever from Sapura or the company's major shareholders, namely, the Public Trustee and Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) on this subject," UMW said in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
PNB is the state investment fund
On Tuesday, Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Sapura had submitted a proposal to the government to buy a stake in UMW.
The government owns a 45 percent stake in UMW.
UMW holds the franchise for the assembly and distribution of Japanese Toyota vehicles in Malaysia, while privately-held Sapura is a telecommunications company.
On Monday, PNB said that it had not received a proposal from Sapura for a buy-in.
Market speculation indicated that the size of the stake Sapura was eyeing could be around 32 percent of UMW's equity.
